findings.title: U1 pin EN is floating / undriven
findings.failure_mode: A floating EN/CHIP_PU leaves the module in an indeterminate reset state — unreliable or no boot.
findings.citation: ESP32-S3-WROOM-1 datasheet + hardware design guidelines: EN (CHIP_PU) must be pulled up (typ. 10k) with a delay cap; it must not float or the module may not boot reliably.

findings.title: U1 pin IO0 has no net for a required 100n
findings.failure_mode: A 1uF (instead of 100nF) cap on IO0 defeats the auto-download/reset sequence — can't flash without manual BOOT.
findings.citation: ESP32 auto-program circuit: IO0 uses a 100nF cap. A 1uF cap here (as on EN) is too large and breaks the auto-download timing.

findings.title: U1 pin EN has no net for a required 10k
findings.failure_mode: Missing EN pull-up => no defined power-on reset delay.
findings.citation: ESP32-S3 hardware design guidelines: EN uses a ~10k pull-up to 3V3 plus a 1uF delay cap (RC reset).

findings.title: U1 pin IO0 has no net for a required 10k
findings.failure_mode: Missing IO0 pull-up can leave the module entering download mode unexpectedly.
findings.citation: ESP32-S3 hardware design guidelines: IO0 (boot strap) needs a pull-up (typ. 10k) so the module boots to flash by default.

findings.title: U1 pin 3V3 is on 'Net-(R31-Pad1)', expected a net containing '3.3'
findings.failure_mode: Module supply off the 3.3V rail is out of spec.
findings.citation: ESP32-S3-WROOM-1 datasheet, Pin definitions (3V3): module supply is 3.3V.

findings.title: U16 output paralleled with ESP32-DevKitC onboard 3V3 regulator via R31 (0Ω)
findings.detail: U16 VOUT (+3.3V) connects through 0Ω R31 to U1 pins 1/2 (3V3). U1 is also fed with +5V on pin 21, so the DevKitC's own onboard LDO drives its 3V3 pins too. The result is two LDO outputs tied directly together with nothing to share the load between them. The AP2112's pinout, its 5V input (within the 6.0V maximum), the EN pin tied high and the decoupling all meet the datasheet.
findings.failure_mode: Whichever regulator sits slightly higher supplies most of the current. U16 may end up carrying all of the ESP32's Wi-Fi current peaks plus the display load, or the two regulators may back-feed each other. That can cause uneven heating or current limiting. Use one source only: either fit R31 so that U16 alone supplies the rail, or remove R31 and keep the two rails separate.

findings.title: DevKit fed from both 5V and 3V3 pins: two 3.3V regulators in parallel
findings.detail: The 5V header pin (U1.21) is tied to +5V, so the DevKit's own LDO makes 3.3V. At the same time the DevKit 3V3 pins (U1.1/U1.2) are tied through the 0 Ω R31 to the board +3.3V rail, which the AP2112K (U16) generates. The datasheet says the 5V pin and the 3V3 pin are mutually exclusive ways to power the board. The way it is wired, the onboard LDO output sits directly in parallel with U16, and when USB is plugged in it also back-feeds +5V.
findings.failure_mode: The two LDOs fight over the shared rail, which causes uneven current sharing, possible reverse current into the regulator with the lower output, and supply sequencing problems. Fix it by removing R31 (leave it unpopulated) or by not feeding the 5V pin.

findings.title: ILI9341 module datasheet unavailable — DS1 not verified
findings.detail: No datasheet could be found for the ILI9341 display module (DS1), so its pinout and electrical requirements could not be checked. One point to look at once a datasheet is added: the backlight LED pin (pin 8) is driven straight from GPIO17. Whether that works depends on whether the module has its own backlight transistor.
findings.failure_mode: An unchecked pinout mismatch or a backlight current higher than the GPIO can supply could leave the display dark or not working.

findings.title: TS5A23157 datasheet unavailable; SW3 not audited against datasheet
findings.detail: No datasheet could be found for SW3 (TS5A23157, module footprint), so its pinout, V+ rating, logic thresholds and NC/NO switching behaviour could not be checked. Please add the PDF so the audit can be completed.
findings.failure_mode: A pinout or wiring error on the module, such as NC and NO being swapped, would go unnoticed and could send the wrong signal path to the CH1/CH2 attenuators.

dropped.title: DevKit powered on both 5V pin and 3V3 pin simultaneously (paralleled regulators)
dropped.detail:
U1 pin 21 (5V) is fed from the board +5V rail (U3 LM7805), and U1 pins 1/2 (3V3) are tied through 0Ω R31 to the board +3.3V rail driven by U16 AP2112K-3.3. The DevKit's onboard LDO therefore drives its 3V3 output directly into the AP2112 output. The datasheet says the 5V and 3V3 supply inputs are mutually exclusive. Also, when USB is plugged in, the DevKit's USB 5V meets the board's +5V.

Second opinion (unsure): The netlist shows only R31.1 on the DevKit 3V3 net and gives no value for R31 or any connection from R31.2 to U16's output, so the 0Ω tie to the AP2112 rail is unverified; even if it exists, two 3.3V LDOs in parallel normally do not damage each other (LDOs source current but do not sink it), and 'mutually exclusive' on p.106 is a usage recommendation rather than proof of a board-killing fault.
dropped.failure_mode: Two LDO outputs fight each other, which causes back-feeding, uneven current sharing and possible regulator stress. Plugging in USB can back-feed the 7805 output.

dropped.title: U15 channel B (pins 5,6,7) left unconnected
dropped.detail: Only amplifier 1 of the dual OPA2810 in U15 is used, as a unity-gain buffer driving CENTER_BIAS. The netlist shows no connection at all on VIN2+ (pin 5), VIN2- (pin 6) or VO2 (pin 7). If amplifier 2 is not needed, connect it as a buffer (tie pin 7 to pin 6) and tie pin 5 to ground or to a mid-supply voltage.
dropped.failure_mode: A floating FET-input amplifier can drift to a rail or oscillate. That raises supply current and couples noise into amplifier 1 and the CENTER_BIAS reference.
dropped.excerpt: VIN2+ 5 I Amplifier 2 noninverting input pin

dropped.title: No datasheet available for DS1 (ILI9341 module)
dropped.detail: No datasheet could be found for DS1, the ILI9341 14-pin SPI TFT/touch module, so its pins couldn't be checked against the manufacturer's spec. These connections still need a review against the module's datasheet: the LED backlight pin is driven directly from GPIO17, so check how much current it draws. The display and touch controller share SCK and MOSI (GPIO4 and GPIO5), the display's SDO pin is left unconnected, and VCC is on +3.3V.
dropped.failure_mode: Without the datasheet, problems such as backlight current above what the GPIO can supply, or an unexpected supply or level requirement, can't be ruled out.

dropped.title: TS5A23157 datasheet unavailable; SW3 not audited against it
dropped.detail: No datasheet could be found for SW3 (TS5A23157), so its pinout, supply rating (+3.3V on V+), and signal ranges on COM1/COM2 (AD9833 outputs) could not be checked against the manufacturer's specifications.
dropped.failure_mode: A pinout or rating error on SW3 would go unnoticed. That could break the routing of the function-generator signals.
